title: Dedicated capacity weekly prep - Maya Patel - 2026-03-08
body:
Weekly prep for dedicated capacity sync (Mon 2026-03-09)

Context / goal:
- Quick sync to align on GPU pool forecasts, upcoming reservation renewals, and autoscaling policy tweaks before Q2 sales pushes.
- Surface any risks to meeting customer SLAs and identify owners for follow-ups.

Attendees (planned): Jordan, Samir, Priya, Evan (ops), me
Duration: 30-40min

Agenda:
1) Quick numbers (5m)
   - Total reserved GPUs (current): 1,280 A100-equivalent (across pools)
   - Current utilized capacity: ~72% average over last 7 days
   - Peak 1-hr utilization last 24h: 91% (region-us-west)
   - On-demand / burst capacity used last week: ~48 GPU-hours (small)
2) Upcoming reservations & renewals (8m)
   - ACME Corp reserved pool (120 GPUs) renewal due 2026-03-20 — ask sales for commitment update
   - Two pilot customers (RetailX, FinAlytics) request +40 GPUs each starting Apr 1 (probable)
   - Reserved expiry: 64 GPUs (eu-central) on 2026-04-05 — consider early renewal or migration plan
3) Autoscaling and policy tuning (8m)
   - Current policy: scale-up threshold 85% sustained over 5m; scale-down after 10m at <60%
   - Observed oscillation on multi-tenant pools during morning spike (6-9am PST)
   - Proposal: increase scale-up to 88% and add predictive warm-up for scheduled customer jobs
   - Discuss cost impact vs latency risk if we pre-warm
4) Short-term forecast (5m)
   - Expected net delta for next 30 days: +200 GPUs (commits + pilots) vs -40 (decommissions) = +160
   - Immediate capacity pressure in us-west and eu-central; propose shifting 32 GPUs from general pool to reserved buffer
5) Action items & owners (4m)

Quick notes / diagnostics:
- Samir: can we get per-model seq-length distribution for RetailX traffic? Their requests show higher average seq len which impacts throughput.
- Jordan: run a 1-hour load test on the ACME reserved pool with model variant llama-3-8b-q4 run (simulate 10% tail traffic) — capture P99 latency and GPU utilization.
- Priya: confirm billing cadence for pilot customers (monthly vs quarterly) — affects finance approval for early capacity.
- Ops: check automated fallback config — ensure that when reserved pools hit 95% we trigger routing to compatible hosted variants (with SLO notes to customers).

Draft forecast (numbers rough, to refine in sheet):
- Baseline reserved: 1,280 GPUs
- New commitments expected: +160 GPUs over 30d
- Buffer target: 10% of committed = ~144 GPUs
- Suggest short-term shift: allocate 32 GPUs from general to reserved buffer (temporary)

Risks / unknowns:
- Sales hasn't signed ACME renewal; if they churn we lose 120 GPU commit and revenue — contingency: move 64 GPUs back to general pool and open capacity to pilots
- EU pool expiry 2026-04-05 might coincide with FinAlytics pilot; coordinate with infra to avoid region imbalance
- Autoscale oscillation could cause transient latency spikes; need to tweak cooldowns and add hysteresis

Action items (clear owners & dates):
- Jordan Lee: run ACME reserved pool load test + upload perf log to CONFLUENCE-DC-2026-02 (due 2026-03-10)
- Samir Rao: export RetailX seq-len distribution + recommended quantization profile (due 2026-03-11)
- Priya Nair: confirm pilot billing cadence and finance go/no-go for early capacity (due 2026-03-12)
- Evan Green (ops): implement temporary shift of 32 GPUs to reserved buffer and monitor utilization (start 2026-03-09, report 2026-03-11)
- Maya Patel (me): update dedicated capacity forecast spreadsheet and send to sales as FYI (sheet link in artifacts) (done 2026-03-09)

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Re-check autoscaler metrics pipeline; last time we had missing sample points during redeploys — add alert if metric gaps > 2m
- Consider adding a predictive scaler experiment for scheduled batch jobs (RetailX has 10am daily runs)
- Flag to product: customers are asking for clearer SLAs on reserved vs burst capacity — product should prepare a short FAQ we can share with sales

Meeting prep checklist (what I'll bring):
- Updated forecast sheet (baseline + scenario + buffer)
- ACME contract summary (sales notes)
- Recent 7-day utilization graphs (per-region)
- Current autoscale policy config (link to ENG-1423)

Links/refs:
- Forecast sheet: CONFLUENCE-DC-2026-02 (linked_artifacts)
- Autoscale ticket: ENG-1423
- Runtime PR for predictive warm-up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/298

"Notes-style" items (scratch):
- If we pre-warm 32 GPUs for morning spike cost ~ +$7k/month but reduces P99 by ~120ms for affected traffic — calculate ROI if ACME/Fin customers have latency SLOs
- Check KMS/HSM impact if moving private-hosted pools between regions (security sign-off ok?)

End.
